chain.label: AA DC-10 manual lacked mandatory directional-control procedures
chain.trigger: American Airlines did not have procedures for: 1) Holding forward pressure on the yoke after touchdown; 2) Not using the handwheel steering control at high speeds; ... 4) Coming out of reverse into forward thrust to regain directional control.

chain.label: Cabin emergency lighting battery packs improperly serviced
chain.trigger: the tap wire or primary lead was incorrectly soldered onto all four battery packs. In addition, individual battery cells were out of the original factory-assembled sequence.

chain.label: Line of thunderstorms/heavy rain crossing DFW during approach and landing
chain.trigger: a line of moderate to heavy rain showers and thunderstorms was crossing runway 17L as AAL102 was landing

chain.label: Gusty, shifting right crosswind/wind surge during touchdown and rollout
chain.trigger: wind gusts of 25 to 32 knots ... at the CFA

caused_by.evidence: a wind surge was associated with the line of showers and thunderstorms moving across the airport

chain.label: Captain overrode first officer's go-around call at ~40-50 ft and took control to land
chain.trigger: The first officer stated, 'I'm gonna go around.' The captain stated, 'No, no, no, I got it.'

caused_by.evidence: These data would indicate that AAL102 was subjected to a direct right crosswind of 25 to 30 knots, when the first officer stated, 'I'm gonna go around'

chain.label: Captain released the yoke to use handwheel steering and kept full reverse thrust instead of correcting with rudder/forward pressure
chain.trigger: He released the control column and used the nosewheel steering handwheel control ... he did not take the engines out of reverse thrust

caused_by.evidence: the captain took control of the airplane and landed the airplane
the airplane's nose turned to the right, most likely due to the right cross wind acting upon the vertical stabilizer
American Airlines did not have procedures for ... using the handwheel steering control ... coming out of reverse into forward thrust to regain directional control

chain.label: Airplane failed to respond to control inputs and continued drifting right of centerline
chain.trigger: there was little input into the flight controls to maintain the airplane on the runway ... 'there was nothing we could do but hang on'

caused_by.evidence: below 118 knots there was very little input into the rudder ... virtually no input into the elevator or ailerons

chain.label: Airplane departed the runway, crossed taxiway 3S, gear collapsed in soft soil, fuel line ruptured and fire ignited
chain.trigger: the airplane departed the right side of runway 17 left ... The main fuel supply line to the No. 2 engine was found fractured

caused_by.evidence: the airplane came to rest, upright, about 2,607 feet from the departure end of 17L and about 250 feet from the right edge of the runway

chain.label: Two serious and 38 minor injuries during a hampered emergency evacuation
chain.trigger: Two passengers received serious injuries, and 35 passengers, 1 flightcrew member, and 2 cabincrew members received minor injuries during the evacuation

caused_by.evidence: the fire affected the urgency of passenger egress because it could be seen glowing through the left windows of a darkened aft cabin
the power and charge level was not sufficient to illuminate the overhead and door emergency lighting system
